subject: general
question: At what rate (in percentage) per annum will ₹1,300 give ₹650 as simple interest in 10 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Simple Interest** for 10 years is ₹650.

Interest for 1 year = 650 ÷ 10 = ₹65.

**Rate** % = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100

Rate % = (65 ÷ 1300) × 100 = 5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal** (P) = ₹1,300

**Simple Interest** (SI) = ₹650

**Time** (T) = 10 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f67e08c3d87ed0ebc118422ac930d826ca8a6adfbcdc5c0f3e63364414813a43.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 650 = (1300 × R × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ 650 = 130 × R

⇒ R = 650 ÷ 130

⇒ R = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Basics

Interest remains constant every year in **Simple Interest**. Total Amount = Principal + SI.

Effective Rate of Interest

Effective Rate for the entire period is R × T %. Here, 5% × 10 = 50%, which matches ₹650 being 50% of ₹1,300.

Relationship with Compound Interest

For the first year (or first compounding period), **Simple Interest** and **Compound Interest** are always equal.
